analysis:
I examined the change to LocalTokenizerLoader.swift (head lines 73-74, 81 and 101-138) and the docs/developer/test.md additions.

The bridge now builds a map of `<0xHH>` token IDs at init. It probes each of the 256 byte tokens with convertTokenToId and checks the round trip with convertIdToToken. It keeps the map only when a lone byte token decodes to an empty string, so a fixed upstream decoder turns the workaround off.

decode() then walks the output IDs backwards. It collects held-back trailing byte tokens and appends them with String(decoding:as: UTF8). Invalid UTF-8 is replaced with U+FFFD rather than causing a crash.

The change affects output-text correctness only, on the provider side of TB-007. It does not touch:
- encryption or attestation (A-001 sealing, T-008 fail-closed encryption)
- cache scoping (T-041 cacheSalt, SSD keys)
- prompt encoding or the prompt token cache

No new trust boundary or external input surface is added. Tokenizer files remain operator-controlled, which is pre-existing under T-012/TB-003.

Availability is a minor point. When skipSpecialTokens is true, the backward loop calls upstream.decode once per trailing special or byte token. For outputs that are long runs of special tokens, a streaming caller could see quadratic cost. This is model-output driven and bounded by max_tokens, so I see no concrete exploitable regression.

The docs changes describe tests and add no security claims that conflict with the threat model. The cluster prefix tenant partition text is existing context in unit 12, outside the changed range 551-561.

Open question for integration: whether DetokenizerV2 correctly holds back trailing U+FFFD in streaming, as the code comment assumes. That source was not supplied; it affects correctness, not security.
